CausalChain: Fibrotic liver disease -> Increased ECM stiffness -> Activation of integrin β1/FAK in cancer cells & integrin β5/FAK/MEK/ERK in liver-resident macrophages -> Cancer cell malignant behavior and macrophage M2 polarization -> Secretion of TGF-β, LOXL2 and ECM remodeling enzymes -> Further increase in matrix stiffness -> Reinforcement of tumor-promoting microenvironment -> Activation of compensatory YAP/TAZ signaling
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in the setting of fibrotic liver disease, increased ECM stiffness initiates a dual mechanotransduction cascade that differentially engages cancer cells and liver-resident macrophages. In cancer cells, the heightened matrix rigidity predominantly activates the integrin β1/FAK pathway, reinforcing tumorigenic traits such as enhanced proliferation, migration, and EMT. Simultaneously, in liver-resident macrophages, we propose that ECM stiffness activates an integrin β5/FAK/MEK/ERK signaling cascade that drives macrophage polarization toward an immunosuppressive, M2-like state. This polarization results in the secretion of TGF-β, LOXL2, and other ECM remodeling enzymes, which further exacerbate matrix stiffness, thereby sustaining a feed-forward loop that supports a tumor-promoting microenvironment. Additionally, sustained high stiffness conditions trigger compensatory activation of YAP/TAZ signaling across both cell types. To validate and potentially interrupt this deleterious cycle, we propose leveraging state-of-the-art technologies including real-time single-cell transcriptomics and advanced stiffness-sensing modalities. Therapeutically, a regimen tightly integrating inhibitors targeting the integrin β1 and β5 pathways together with YAP/TAZ modulators could repolarize macrophages from an immunosuppressive to a pro-inflammatory state and reduce cancer cell malignancy, offering a novel strategy to mitigate hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
Abstract: In fibrotic liver disease, the alteration in extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics leads to a complex interplay between tumor cells and the immune microenvironment. Our revised hypothesis posits that increased ECM stiffness triggers a dual mechanotransduction response: in cancer cells, it activates the well-established integrin β1/FAK pathway, promoting malignant behaviors such as proliferation, migration, and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition; concurrently, in liver-resident macrophages, ECM stiffness engages integrin β5/FAK/MEK/ERK signaling, which we propose biases these cells toward an M2-like, immunosuppressive phenotype. These M2-like macrophages secrete TGF-β, LOXL2, and additional ECM remodeling enzymes, further reinforcing matrix stiffening and establishing a self-perpetuating feed-forward loop. Moreover, sustained high stiffness conditions induce compensatory YAP/TAZ activation in both cell types. Utilizing cutting-edge real-time single-cell transcriptomics and high-resolution stiffness-sensing technologies, we intend to monitor and dissect these interactions. We further propose that a combinatorial therapeutic regimen targeting both integrin β1 and β5 signaling in tandem with YAP/TAZ modulation can disrupt this harmful circuit, repolarize macrophages, and diminish cancer cell malignancy, thereby mitigating the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis retains the original causal chain by linking fibrotic liver disease with increased ECM stiffness, which activates integrin β1/FAK signaling in cancer cells and integrin β5/FAK/MEK/ERK signaling in macrophages leading to malignant and immunosuppressive behaviors, respectively. It further preserves the concept of TGF-β, LOXL2, and ECM remodeling enzyme secretion fueling additional matrix stiffness, reinforcing a tumor-promoting microenvironment that culminates in compensatory YAP/TAZ activation. However, the new formulation addresses the review comments by critically acknowledging the strong empirical base for the integrin β1 pathway while situating the integrin β5 pathway in macrophages as an emerging area with potential cross-talk. It also enhances practical implementability by explicitly integrating advanced real-time single-cell transcriptomics and stiffness-sensing technologies for monitoring these events, thus refining the therapeutic strategy to include nuanced and contemporary approaches for disrupting the pathogenic feedback loop.
